answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because nebula only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, harbor is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any lotus approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
